---
title: "ADR 0002: Introduce .NET components in the NADABAS repository"
---

## Status and date

Initial implementation decision, 2026-10-27. Production installation and
database migration remain future decisions requiring runtime evidence.

## Context

NADABAS is an Excel/VBA application with shared database and workbook state.
The migration must permit small releases while preserving current workflows.
Installation and version checking are more bounded than data writes or batch
execution. VBA and .NET changes will initially share maintainers, contracts,
test fixtures and release compatibility requirements.

## Decision

Keep the .NET source under `dotnet/` in the existing repository, with its own
solution, SDK policy, tests and CI workflow. Use C# and .NET 10 LTS. Start with
a read-only executable for setup diagnostics; implement installation only
after explicit planning, signature verification and recovery tests exist.

Keep Excel events, ribbon, forms and session initialization in VBA. A later
process adapter will exchange versioned data messages. Do not move Excel
objects, module-level ADO cursors or shared globals across that boundary.
Migrate complete operations, with comparative tests against the VBA baseline.

## Installation and update target (2026-10-28)

The maintainer clarified the intended user experience: users install NADABAS
once, subsequent updates happen automatically, and IT can control deployment.
This is the product target, not functionality delivered by the current prototype.

The implementation must provide:

- A normal first-install flow that installs the required components and registers
  the Excel add-in without manual file copying. End users do not need a .NET SDK.
- Automatic updates from an approved release source, with publisher and package
  validation and explicit compatibility between the add-in and .NET components.
- IT policy that takes precedence over user defaults: defer or disable automatic
  updates, pin an approved version, and select an approved release source/channel.
- Deferred activation of add-in updates until Excel is closed. Do not close a
  user's Excel session or replace a loaded add-in to apply an update.
- Verified backup and recovery for failed updates, preservation of user settings
  and data, and a visible installed version and update result.
- Repair and uninstall flows that remove application components without deleting
  user workbooks or databases.

Per-user versus machine-wide installation, packaging technology, update trigger,
release hosting and the IT policy mechanism remain design decisions. An automatic
update may still run an installer internally; the user should not have to repeat
the manual installation procedure for each release. Existing Office security
policy continues to apply.

The next implementation milestone is an upgrade rehearsal between two explicitly
identified test packages, including Excel-open deferral, failed-update recovery
and IT-policy precedence. Production automatic download and installation follow
package trust and upgrade acceptance checks. Database regression checks remain
necessary before replacing the existing installer for users.

## Consequences

One pull request can change a contract and both consumers, with coordinated
review and compatibility tests. Separate folders and CI keep toolchains clear.
No Python runtime is required for the .NET executable. Runtime releases can
later be versioned independently within the same repository, but must declare
which VBA/add-in versions they support. JSON schema version 1 currently covers
diagnostic output only; it is not yet a production VBA integration contract.

CI success does not replace Office, driver, signing or database acceptance.
Keep database schema unchanged during the first increments. Do not equate a
move to .NET with removal of Excel licensing or a cross-platform Excel client.

## Alternatives

- **Separate repository now:** adds cross-repository coordination before the
  boundary is stable. Reconsider when the component has independent ownership,
  release cadence, access requirements or consumers outside NADABAS.
- **COM DLL first:** possible, but adds registration, runtime and Office
  bitness considerations before the deployment model is established.
- **Complete rewrite:** delays feedback and changes too much behaviour at once.

This is a context-specific decision, not a universal rule that one repository
is always preferable. See the [local setup guide](../developer-guide/dotnet-local-setup.md)
and [component scope](../../dotnet/README.md).
